thread:
Alex: quick heads-up — we're planning a roll to remove PodSecurityPolicy from tenant-silo clusters and rely solely on NetworkPolicies + RBAC for isolation in private deployments. want to surface any gotchas for customers and ops.

Maria: high-level q: will audit logs still capture deny/accept decisions at the kube-proxy/netpol level? customers need proof of isolation for audits.

Devon: also: KMS integration question — if we move to network-policy-first, do we need new key access patterns for the kubelet/node agent that writes tenant-level audit blobs to our S3 on-prem mirror? rotation + least-priv is tricky.

Rukmini: summary from infra side: PSP -> netpol transition is OK but you must ensure: (1) egress blocking netpols exist (2) hostNetwork workloads are gated by nodeSelector & taints (3) audit export path uses short-lived creds.

Rukmini: quick example netpol we propose for tenant pods (deny-by-default, allow app-to-app + prometheus scraping):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-default-deny
  namespace: tenant-abc
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  ingress: []
  egress: []
```

Devon: for audit export creds: recommend we issue ephemeral role tokens via our private STS service; node agent exchanges mTLS + node identity for short creds. KMS keys should be used to sign blobs, not to directly encrypt each upload.

Maria: retention question: some of our regulated customers need immutable logs for 7 years. How do we provide that on private infra without shipping master keys?

Rukmini: two options: (A) customer brings their own HSM and we store wrapped keys + audit artifacts encrypted client-side, or (B) we provide an immutable object store appliance (append-only) with customer-controlled rotate/passphrase. both need a legal/contract path.

Devon: related vuln triage: flagged CVE in CNI plugin (hostport handling) — if customer still uses hostPort, isolation bypass possible. we should make hostPort a gated flag in our private deploy manifest and default to false.

Alex: +1 to gating hostPort. Ops: can we add a preflight check that scans manifests for hostPort + hostNetwork + privileged containers?

infra-bot: preflight-checker: scan started for cluster tenant-abc. found 2 manifests with hostPort. details: pod/web-legacy uses hostPort: 8080; pod/metrics-bridge uses hostNetwork: true.

ops-oncall: incident note — if we detect hostNetwork after rollout, our runbook should: 1) create an isolation netpol for that namespace, 2) rotate node agent creds, 3) notify customer + security with suspected blast-radius. confirmable?

Rukmini: runbook sketch:
- Detect hostNetwork/hostPort post-deploy (automated watcher)
- Apply immediate emergency NetPolicy (egress-deny + limited ingress from control-plane IPs)
- Quarantine node(s) via cordon + taint, schedule migration, revoke ephemeral tokens
- Run image provenance & vuln scan for pods on those nodes
- Notify SOC + customer with timeline and evidence (audit blobs)

Maria: for evidence, we need the audit blobs signed and time-stamped. who owns the signing key in private deployments?

Devon: prefer model: customer KMS holds master key, we get a subordinate signing key wrapped by customer's KMS. that way we can sign while customer can revoke/rotate. document this pattern for SOC review.

Alex: next action items:
- Rukmini: add hostPort/hostNetwork gating to private-deploy manifests + preflight (ETA 2d)
- Devon: draft ephemeral creds flow + KMS wrapping pattern (ETA 3d)
- Maria: confirm regulatory retention options and contract language (ETA 5d)
- Ops: add runbook stub to incidents repo and hook automated watcher to alerts (ETA 4d)

ops-oncall: acked. I'll schedule a tabletop for this Friday at 10am PT. tagging @all who work customer private deployments. :calendar:

Alex: thanks. if anyone has customer-specific constraints (airgap HSM, no outbound), drop them here and we'll triage per-customer runbooks.
